data.title: Wall Street rebound faces high bar as earnings risks mount
data.description:
Wall Street’s recent selloff may prove difficult to reverse, with weakening earnings drivers threatening to limit a recovery even as investor risk appetite has fallen sharply, according to TS Lombard.

The research firm said equity markets had come under pressure lately as a more hawkish Federal Reserve and concerns over the profitability of heavy artificial intelligence spending weighed on sentiment. 

A brief improvement following Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO has failed to gain traction, with technology stocks facing another round of selling.

TS Lombard said the recent deterioration in risk appetite appeared excessive but argued that the economic backdrop for corporate earnings had become less supportive. Its risk appetite indicator had fallen to -62.6, while the Global Cross Asset Risk Sentiment Index stood at 38.5.

The firm also noted that the recent reduction in investor positioning had been more moderate than during the 2022 downturn, suggesting markets could struggle to recover their losses before year-end.

The firm identified several headwinds for U.S. corporate earnings. Fiscal policy is expected to weigh on economic growth next year, while growth in hyperscaler capital expenditure, a key driver of corporate profits, appears to have peaked.

TS Lombard also warned that a tightening U.S. labor market could push wage growth higher next year, putting further pressure on corporate profitability.

The firm added that the dollar’s recent appreciation could lead to stronger negative earnings revisions in the U.S., creating another obstacle for equities. Its charts show hyperscaler capex growth on a 12-month forward basis turning lower from its recent peak, while indicators of U.S. hiring and wage growth point to a labor market that could put renewed pressure on costs.

The combination leaves a high bar for a swift market rebound, TS Lombard said. While the selloff has reflected a sharp deterioration in sentiment, the underlying drivers of earnings have also weakened, making it harder for stocks to regain lost ground quickly.

The firm said equities could struggle to recover their recent losses this year, despite the possibility that risk appetite has fallen too far.

data.title: HSBC: AI will remain as the key market engine into 2027
data.description:
HSBC sees artificial intelligence as the dominant force shaping markets in 2027, with adoption set to accelerate as models become more powerful. The bank expects this shift to deliver measurable productivity gains and spark a wider wave of innovation across industries.

It argues that the recent drop in IT price-to-earnings ratios to five-year lows signals excessive caution about near-term AI monetization and an undue focus on short-term results. Attention instead centers on the opportunities likely to emerge over the next six to twelve months. 

HSBC noted that adoption remains early. The average U.S. company currently spends only $16 per employee each month on AI, leaving considerable room for expansion. Productivity improvements should pick up further in 2027 for three reasons: models continue to grow more capable, costs per token keep falling, and usage moves beyond chatbots toward AI agents and physical AI applications. 

On this basis, HSBC holds a risk-on stance, viewing sustained AI deployment as a source of real economic gains that should continue to support market performance.

data.title: 4 stocks to watch on Friday: NVDA, ANT, UBER, and MU
data.description:
Stock index futures surged on Friday as Wall Street looked to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

Here are four stocks to watch on the day:

Nvidia (NVDA) shares rose 4% in premarket trading Friday, ahead of a shortened trading session, although the gains offered little evidence that the chipmaker had put a volatile week behind it. The stock surged 31% on Monday following Jensen Huang’s dramatic return as chief executive and president, but subsequently surrendered some of those gains, falling 5.9% on Tuesday and closing 3.91% lower on Wednesday after dropping as much as 7% during the session.

Anthropic (ANT) shares rose 3.3% in premarket trading Friday as the newly listed company looked to recover from a rocky start on the public markets. The stock snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, gaining 1.08% ahead of the Thanksgiving break, but its losses over the first five trading sessions had pushed it to $82.79, below its $83 IPO price. Anthropic opened at $111.50 and reached an intraday high of $115.10 during its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19.

Uber Technologies (UBER) shares gained 1.36% in early trading after the company announced the final results of its voluntary public takeover offer for the remaining registered shares of Delivery Hero SE through its indirect wholly-owned subsidiary, Uber International Technologies II Corporation. Uber secured approximately 87.13% of Delivery Hero’s total share capital by the end of the additional acceptance period on November 24, 2026, with the transaction closing anticipated in the second half of 2027.

Micron Technology (MU) shares climbed 6.07% in premarket trading Friday, while SK Hynix and Samsung also drew attention after GF Securities lowered its 2027 dynamic random-access memory price forecasts amid order reductions from China. The firm now expects contract prices to rise 6%, 3%, 0%, and 0% across the four quarters of 2027, down from previous estimates of 10%, 7%, 5%, and 3%, citing TrendForce data pointing to weaker demand from Chinese cloud service providers.

data.title: Chip stocks rebound to cap a volatile week
data.description:
Chip and AI stocks gained on before the bell ahead of a shortened trading session Friday.

Nvidia (NVDA) shares were up 2.4%, looking to close out a volatile week with a winning session. The stock has swung sharply over the past three sessions that included a record-breaking 31% surge on Monday, followed by two straight sessions of losses in which stock shed roughly 10% value. 

Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) gained more than 4%; the stock has lost roughly 11% so far this week. 

Broadcom (AVGO), Amkor (AMKR), Applied Materials (AMAT), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM), Intel (INTC), KLA (KLAC), and GlobalFoundries (GFS) were also down between 3% and 6%.

AI infrastructure stocks rebounded too, with Nebius (NBIS), CoreWeave (CRWV), and IREN (IREN) gaining between 5% and 8%. The stocks have been in focus following media reports that Nvidia chip sellers are warning neocloud providers they could lose access to chips if they rent computing capacity to Chinese companies.

Among memory stocks, Sandisk (SNDK) gained the most, trading more than 9% higher. Micron (MU), Western Digital (WDC), SK Hynix's U.S.-listed shares (SKHY), and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) all gained between 5% and 8%. 

Optical technology stocks, which provide equipment for moving data through AI data centers, also traded higher. Corning (GLW), Lumentum (LITE), Coherent (COHR), and Ciena (CIEN) gained between 5% and 7%.

Hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Meta (META) gained between 2% and 5%.

data.title: European luxury braces for another bumpy and uneven year—J.P. Morgan
data.description:
The European luxury space could face another challenging year, says J.P. Morgan analysts Chiara Battistini and Wendy Liu, as consumer spending is still resilient but discriminating.

This will be especially notable in China, where high net worth individuals will continue to spend while "aspirational customers" will shift their share of wallet towards brands with sharp, authentic execution.

The analysts see jewelry and ready-to-wear remaining as bright spots, while luxury goods will experience a “bumpy” year as demand will be driven by brand strength.

Against this backdrop, their stock picking remains selective, calling out Richemont (CFRHF) (CFRUY) as a top pick in luxury.

Battistini and Liu remain Overweight on Brunello Cucinelli (BCUCF) (BCUCY), Zegna Group (ZGN), and Moncler (MONRF) (MONRY).

Swatch (SWGAY)(SWGAF) (SWGNF) and Pandora (PNDZF) (PNDRY) (upgraded to Overweight) are both placed on J.P. Morgan’s Positive Catalyst Watch with Pandora buoyed by declining silver prices and signs of better brand momentum.

Kering (PPRUF) (PPRUY) retains its Underweight rating as the “most challenging story in leather goods,” given that the Gucci revamp is expected to take longer than hoped and will likely delay a return to growth to the second half of next year.

In sporting goods, Puma (PMMAF) was downgraded to Underweight and adidas (ADDYY) (ADDDF) to Neutral amid sector headwinds. 

Lastly, the analysts remain cautious towards both LVMH Moet Hennessy-Louis Vuitton (LVMHF) (LVMUY) and Hermès (HESAY) (HESAF) with both lacking an imminent catalyst for re-rating.

data.title: Goods trade deficit unexpectedly widens in October; Wholesale and retail inventories rise
data.description:
October international trade in goods (advance): -$149.5B vs. -$133.0B consensus and -$135.1B in September, according to data released by the U.S. Census Bureau on Friday.

Wholesale inventories, adjusted: +0.9% to $1,023.4B vs. +0.7% consensus and $1,014.3B prior.

Retail inventories, adjusted: +0.8% to $893.2B vs. $886.2B prior.

data.title: Carlsberg plans an IPO for its India unit
data.description:
Carlsberg India, the country's second-largest brewer, plans to sell up to 86.4M shares, or about 15% of the company, through an entirely secondary offering. That will mean an infusion of cash for Danish parent Carlsberg (CABGY). The latest reports say the IPO could raise as much as $600M at a $4B valuation. The IPO could launch as early as December.   

The Securities and Exchange Board of India approved the IPO, which had been filed under its confidential pre-filing route. Carlsberg India reported revenue of 87.09B rupees for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company runs seven breweries and holds a 21.9% market share across 16 key states and union territories in India.

Looking ahead, Carlsberg (CABGY) shareholders will still benefit from the unit's growth, and the results in India will be public and closely watched by the market.

data.title: Weight Watchers uses $10M cash to retire $16.3M in loan debt
data.description:
• WW International (WW) announced on Friday that it used $10M in cash to retire approximately $16.3M of outstanding term loan debt through a discounted prepayment offer.

  • The company said the debt reduction, combined with earlier repayments, has lowered its total debt by 12.4% this year.

data.title: Columbia Financial CFO Thomas Splaine to step down
data.description:
Columbia Financial (CLBK) on Friday said Thomas Splaine is set to step down from the role of executive vice president and CFO, effective December 18.

Splaine decided to resign for personal reasons.

Shares were 1.38% lower at $10.74 during pre-market trading.

Senior Executive Vice President and Chief Banking Officer Dennis Gibney has been appointed to the additional post of interim CFO.
